steps.what: Assess the actual emergency aboard the motorboat, people at risk, vessel condition and immediate surroundings before choosing the safety response.
inputs: Actual emergency, people and vessel conditions

steps.what: Direct the actual crew and people aboard through the immediate safety operations, giving live instructions, checking understanding and changing directions as the emergency develops.
outputs: Actual directed emergency response and live acknowledgements

steps.what: Monitor the actual effects of the safety operations and reassess people, vessel and surroundings, maintaining or revising the live emergency directions.
inputs: Actual response and changing conditions after s2
outputs: Actual updated safety priorities and ongoing supervision

tasks.design: Keep emergency assessment and live direction with the operator. OTHER means actual onboard safety equipment and instruments. An existing emergency checklist may support recall; no newly required written incident record, copied checklist or outgoing distress-message workflow is assumed within this direction task. Live spoken crew instructions are the actual conversation, not a proposed autonomous external transaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The response depends on actual people, boat movement and damage at the moment of the emergency.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing checklists can support recall but remove no established action in this baseline.
tasks.still_hard: A direction can become inappropriate before its physical effect is complete.
tasks.human_edge: Prioritise people and adapt clear instructions to actual behaviour.

ambition.what: Direct the existing emergency safety response.

tasks.altitude: Understand and practise the actual emergency roles and hold conditions.

evidence.claim: An emergency checklist does not establish a reduction in actual assessment, crew direction or monitoring.

assumptions: No distinct manual written report, re-key or outgoing system message is established within this live direction task; none is added as a trailing step.
Crew response is the existing operation and no crew labour saving is claimed.
No unattended emergency response or free transcription is proposed.
unknowns: Actual boat emergency procedures and separately performed communications
research_questions: Observe a drill and identify any real separate record or send action before proposing a software change.

already_counted.description: Actual emergency assessment, live direction and reassessment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: After separating assessment, actual verbal direction and monitoring, no existing written output, re-key or system send is evidenced for this task. Native checklist recall does not remove those actions; all work is retained without inventing a record or a remote emergency system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the actual available crew, readiness and required boat activities with the crew members before assigning work.
inputs: Actual crew availability, readiness and current vessel work

steps.what: Organise the actual crew activities and choose who will perform each activity, taking account of actual experience, workload and changing vessel conditions.
Direct the crew members through their actual activities, confirm the instructions are understood and adjust them through live supervision and feedback.
outputs: Actual directed crew work and revised instructions where needed

tasks.design: Retain the actual coordination of a small boat crew. OTHER is existing onboard communication and operating equipment. A native roster or task list was considered, but no repeated written roster preparation, copied work order or formal completion record is evidenced here. Do not add such records solely to generate a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same available person can be suitable for one actual activity and unsuitable for another as the vessel conditions change.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task displays may assist recall but do not remove the live allocation and direction established here.
tasks.still_hard: Fatigue, understanding and unexpected physical work are not settled by a static roster.
tasks.human_edge: Notice overload and communicate adjustments that the crew can actually execute.

ambition.what: Organise and direct the existing crew work.

tasks.altitude: Develop clear activity ownership and feedback habits.

evidence.claim: A crew task display does not itself remove live readiness checks, allocation judgement or supervision.

assumptions: The existing work is live crew coordination, with no separately evidenced written roster or completion report.
No new capture programme or supplier scheduling work is hidden outside the graph.
No reduction is assumed from this task's classification or handed to an unchecked sibling.
unknowns: Whether the actual operator prepares a written crew task allocation today
research_questions: Observe an actual crew briefing and separately time any written allocation if one exists.

already_counted.description: Actual crew readiness checks, allocation and live supervision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The split exposes actual readiness conversation, allocation and ongoing direction. Native roster reuse would remove a written action only if one exists; it is not established here. With no actual re-key, record or send evidenced, no labour change is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe the actual navigational hazard and determine what is known, what is uncertain and whether the hazard needs immediate radio attention.
inputs: Actual observed obstruction, vessel or waterway hazard
outputs: Actual hazard observations and urgency assessment

steps.what: Read and check the actual hazard position, observation time and reference on the onboard navigation display, distinguishing the boat's position from the hazard's position.
inputs: Actual navigation display and observed relative position
outputs: Actual operator-selected hazard position and time

steps.what: Transfer the actual operator-selected hazard position, reference and observation time into the existing authority hazard-report form {GOV_PORTAL} using its supported native position import.
inputs: Actual selected hazard position and time from s2
outputs: Draft hazard-report position and time fields

steps.what: Write the actual observed hazard description, extent and uncertainty into {GOV_PORTAL}; the native saved reporter profile supplies only the repeated vessel identity and contact fields.
Check the completed actual hazard report, including coordinate reference, hazard versus vessel position, wording, urgency and authority destination, and authorise that final version for transmission.
inputs: Actual observations and position selection from s1-s2
outputs: Final hazard report and version/destination transmission authorisation

steps.what: Retain the final hazard report in the same {GOV_PORTAL} draft session without changing its content.
outputs: Retained final report ready for actual transmission

steps.what: Transmit the actual final hazard report to the authority through {GOV_PORTAL}, only for the version and destination authorised in s5.
outputs: Actual hazard report sent to the authority

steps.what: Respond to the authority's actual receipt or clarification questions about the reported hazard, keeping new observations distinct from the original report.

tasks.design: For an existing non-immediate authority-form route, use supported native position import and saved reporter details. OTHER means the onboard navigation display and actual radio/phone. Do not infer the hazard's location from the vessel's position. Urgent radio reporting remains immediate and manual; the form route must not delay it or add a second mandatory report. Any content or destination change returns to s5 before transmission.
tasks.previous_blocker: A selected actual hazard coordinate and repeated vessel details can be re-keyed into a separate authority form.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported native coordinate import and a reporter profile can remove the exact re-key, without drafting the hazard observations.
tasks.still_hard: A coordinate may locate the observer rather than the actual obstruction, and a non-urgent form is unsuitable for an immediate danger.
tasks.human_edge: Report only observed facts with accurate position uncertainty and urgency.

ambition.what: Make the existing actual hazard report.

tasks.altitude: Know when each reporting channel is appropriate and how position references transfer.

evidence.claim: Supported exact position import and saved reporter fields can remove re-keying without establishing the hazard's position or replacing urgent radio communication.

assumptions: This is a conditional existing authority-form workflow, not a newly invented report or a claim that all motorboats have portal imports; shares are unmeasured estimates.
The operator supplies the actual hazard position in s2 and actual descriptive facts in s4; neither is a free sensor-derived conclusion.
Only repeated vessel/contact fields, 8% of s4, are removed; short new hazard prose stays human.
If the actual route is radio only, no form or extra drafting record is introduced and all actual reporting remains manual.
unknowns: Actual authority channel, accepted coordinate reference and native import support
research_questions: Inspect an actual report route and verify a selected hazard coordinate can transfer without confusing it with own-boat position.

already_counted.description: Actual hazard observation, position judgement, new description, full final check, retention, send and clarification

incremental.description: Verify saved vessel details and position-import reference after changes

approvals.approved_version: Final hazard report and actual authority destination checked in s5; any change requires s5 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conservative case is immediate radio-only reporting or an authority form without compatible coordinate import/profile fields; no change is deployed and no extra report is created. With the actual supported form route, remove 10 hours coordinate re-key plus 2 hours repeated reporter details, less 1 hour upkeep. New observations, position judgement, final checking and real transmission stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the actual vessel, passengers, vehicles or goods and departure circumstances before overseeing the crossing operation.
inputs: Actual vessel, carried load, crew and waterway conditions
outputs: Actual operational readiness concerns and priorities

steps.what: Oversee the actual operation of the vessel across the river, harbour, lake or coastal water, attending to actual traffic, weather, load and vessel behaviour.
inputs: Actual readiness and priorities from s1
outputs: Actual attended vessel operation and identified deviations

steps.what: Coordinate actual onboard activities and respond to deviations through live instructions and direct checks, adapting the operation to the actual passengers, vehicles or goods carried.
inputs: Actual operation and deviations from s2
outputs: Actual coordinated response and adjusted supervision

steps.what: Check the actual arrival and end of the carrying operation, resolving any remaining immediate vessel or load concern before ending the active oversight.
inputs: Actual arrival and operation state after s2-s3
outputs: Actual completed or continued operational oversight

tasks.design: Retain the active oversight of the actual crossing. OTHER is existing onboard navigation, communications and vessel instruments. Native status displays may aid observation, but no manual copied dashboard, separately written crossing report, ticket reconciliation or manifest preparation is established in this task. No new record or autonomous boat-control transaction is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The operation changes with actual traffic, load behaviour and people aboard.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instruments support actual supervision but do not establish a removable duplicate action here.
tasks.still_hard: A normal instrument display does not show every passenger, vehicle or goods problem.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate vessel behaviour, people and surroundings into immediate supervisory action.

ambition.what: Oversee the existing actual carrying operation.

tasks.altitude: Understand the observation coverage of instruments and direct checks.

evidence.claim: A vessel status display does not itself remove actual supervisory attendance and direct load or passenger checks.

assumptions: This graph allocates active oversight time, not elapsed unattended voyage time.
No separately evidenced manual log write, report or send is included; those are not invented as trailing duties.
Existing navigation runtime is not a new labour saving, and no saving is assigned to an unchecked sibling task.
unknowns: Actual vessel operating procedure and any real separate supervisory record
research_questions: Observe a complete carrying cycle and identify any manual duplicate record before proposing a data-flow change.

already_counted.description: Actual readiness checks, attended supervision, live coordination and arrival checks

incremental.description: No new workflow or equipment proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The actual active oversight has been split into readiness, voyage observation, live coordination and arrival checks. No existing separate written report, re-key or send is established. Native displays remove none of these actual actions; no speculative manifest or log baseline is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep actual vessel and crew responsibility while understanding exact reporting data and channel limits.
role.ambitious_version: An operator who reduces proven hazard-report re-keying while remaining present for actual emergencies, crew activities and carrying operations.
